moat_against: No owned feedgas or pricing power — earnings are the Henry Hub vs global LNG spread; unsold-cargo fee guide swung $9.50-10.50 to $12.50-13.50/MMBtu within 2026
Arbitration overhang: BP and Galp tribunals won (Galp capped at $170M, hearing 2027/28; BP damages pending), Orlen outstanding — trust cost with the largest LNG buyers
Heavy leverage: net debt $31,850M; Q2 2026 interest expense $489M, up 58% YoY
Concentration: two operating sites, both Louisiana Gulf Coast; CP2 execution still ahead
Dual-class governance: VG Partners held ~97.6% of combined voting power (Feb 2026) — Class A holders have no say
Cheniere is larger, investment-grade, and buyers' trusted default counterparty
moat_for: Modular 'design one, build many' trains — faster, cheaper construction; Calcasieu Pass beat SPA obligations in Q2 2026 despite turbine maintenance
91% of 2026 cargoes contracted at $5.05/MMBtu weighted-average liquefaction fee; growing long-term SPA book (ConocoPhillips 20-yr, 1 MTPA from 2030)
Scale and speed: 1,000th cargo ~4 years after first export; Calcasieu Pass and Plaquemines operating, CP2 in construction
Gulf Coast location with U.S. feedgas access and Atlantic-basin shipping
moat_justification: Modular 'design one, build many' liquefaction trains are a genuine structural cost/speed advantage — plants built and commissioned faster than stick-built rivals, 1,000th cargo ~4 years after the first export — and near-term volumes are largely contracted (91% of 2026 cargoes at a $5.05/MMBtu weighted-average fee, new 20-year SPAs still being signed). But the product is a commodity spread (U.S. feedgas vs global LNG prices) with no owned upstream gas and no pricing power, unsold-cargo fee expectations swung by ~$3/MMBtu within 2026, customer trust was damaged by the Calcasieu Pass commissioning-cargo arbitrations (BP and Galp won, Orlen pending), and the balance sheet carries $31,850M of net debt. Durable asset position, cyclical economics — moderate moat, 5/10.
name: Venture Global, Inc.
one_liner: Fast-growing LNG exporter with a real modular-construction edge, moat 5/10, but conservative owner's earnings are negative in every filed year and on TTM (-$2.67/share) because ~$13.8B/yr of build-out capex swallows operating cash flow — Tier F on this screen; no price clears 15% on owner's earnings until construction capex rolls off.
